title: Quasars and Active Galaxies
objective: After this level you can explain how feeding supermassive black holes can outshine whole galaxies.
summary: Most big galaxies hide a supermassive black hole. When it feeds, its glowing disk can outshine the galaxy: a quasar.

cards.headline: Some of the brightest objects in the universe are powered by black holes.
Monsters at the center
cards.body: Most large galaxies have a supermassive black hole at their center. When one pulls in large amounts of gas, the gas spirals in, heats up in a swirling disk and glows fiercely, before it crosses the event horizon.

cards.headline: Brighter than a galaxy
cards.body: A feeding black hole’s glowing disk can outshine all the stars of its galaxy combined. The brightest of these are called quasars. They’re among the most distant and luminous objects known.

cards.fact: The first quasar was identified in 1963.
cards.context: Maarten Schmidt realized that the object 3C 273, which looked like a faint star, was actually extremely distant and enormously luminous.

cards.headline: Quasars: understood
learned: Most big galaxies have a supermassive black hole

options.label: Gas heating up as it spirals toward a supermassive black hole
Millions of supernovae exploding at once
Two galaxies colliding head-on
options.rationale: Collisions can feed a quasar, but the power comes from the black hole.

options.label: A giant star at the galaxy’s center

questions.explanation: Gas swirling into a supermassive black hole heats up and glows, sometimes outshining the whole galaxy.

questions.prompt: Why can a quasar outshine an entire galaxy?

options.label: It is closer to Earth than the galaxy
options.rationale: It’s part of the same galaxy.

options.label: It reflects light from nearby stars
Gas heated around its black hole glows more brightly than all the stars combined
It is made of many bright stars packed together
options.rationale: Its light comes from gas around a black hole.

questions.explanation: The disk of gas falling into a supermassive black hole gets so hot it can outshine all the galaxy’s stars together.

questions.prompt: From Level 75: our galaxy has Sagittarius A*. Why isn’t the Milky Way a quasar?

options.label: Sagittarius A* is too small to be a black hole
The Milky Way is too young
Quasars only exist in elliptical galaxies
Sagittarius A* isn’t pulling in large amounts of gas right now

questions.explanation: A black hole only shines as a quasar while it’s feeding heavily. Sagittarius A* is relatively quiet today.
